key_insight: 2D/3D perovskite interface band alignment is highly chemistry-dependent, with surface termination and ionic composition strongly shifting work function and band offsets.
engineering_relevance: Choosing the right 2D capping layer and 3D composition is critical for controlling passivation, charge extraction, and stability in perovskite solar cells.
method: Atomistic study of (PEA)2PbI4 on mixed-cation/mixed-halide 3D perovskites
Computed work function, electron affinity, and band offsets across cleaved surfaces and interfaces
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preliminary simulations showing work functions, interface potentials, and band offsets vary substantially with surface termination and composition, with valence offsets of about 0.2–0.7 eV and conduction offsets near 0.25 eV.
watch_item: Results are preliminary and computational, so the predicted alignments may change with additional interface reconstructions, defects, or device-level effects not yet included.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
